At fixed beam size and local limits, LinearKnot computes the partition function, BPPs, seven loop-context probabilities, window accessibility, and MFE and $\gamma$-centroid structures in linear time in sequence length.

Its pair probabilities, loop-context probabilities, window accessibility, samples, and representative structures come from one ensemble computed in linear time, and they show where crossing pairs and open windows are likely for a given scaffold.
CapR gives loop profiles: structural-context probabilities that describe whether each base is paired or belongs to a particular loop type \citep{Fukunaga2014-fz}.
These outputs describe local loop types, unpaired windows, and structural variation beyond one MFE prediction.
LinearSampling samples structures according to their Boltzmann probabilities \citep{Zhang2023-ut}, and LinearCapR computes structural-context probabilities \citep{Otagaki2026-ev}.
